fatal_errors: The proposed DSC/XRD/CALPHAD workflow does not reconstruct the target MTP-assisted DFT free-energy perturbation method or its replacement of EAM-based thermodynamic integration.
The stated 2000 K upper limit excludes the refractory TaVCrW target and much of the refractory high-entropy-alloy domain.
Loss of crystalline diffraction peaks and solid lattice-parameter evolution do not by themselves provide an accurate liquid volume or volume discontinuity at melting.
The claimed ±1–2% family-wide accuracy and ±5% liquid-property agreement are not supported by the cited evidence.
Nitrogen is not necessarily chemically inert toward refractory alloy constituents at high temperature.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the same broad observables—melting temperature, fusion thermodynamics, volume change, and liquid properties—but proposes an unrelated experimental strategy. It misses the target material, DFT/FEP framework, MTP training criterion, 0 GPa conditions, electronic and short-range-order contributions, and the reported speed and free-energy benchmarks. Its cited papers establish only general usefulness of DSC, CALPHAD, imaging, or MD; they do not validate simultaneous DSC/synchrotron-XRD measurements at the asserted accuracy across HEAs. Independent levitation measurements could provide a useful falsification test, but the >10% threshold is substantially looser than the claimed accuracy and does not directly benchmark all target quantities. The approach may be feasible for selected lower-melting alloys, but it cannot support the stated family-wide scope or quantitative performance.
